forces.title: Retail Transitioning to Platform-Based, Ecosystem-Centric Digital Commerce
forces.description: The retail industry is undergoing a fundamental shift from transaction-centric, channel-optimized models to relationship-centric, ecosystem-based platforms. These platforms enable interactions among multiple participants like consumers, brands, sellers, logistics, and financial institutions, creating value beyond purchases through network effects. This transformation, driven by technology and AI, emphasizes orchestration over asset ownership, leading to self-sustaining growth engines that are harder to replicate than traditional retail capabilities. This structural change redefines competitive advantage and operational strategies for e-commerce platforms.
forces.source_title: From commerce to platform : Reimagining retail as an intelligent ecosystem

forces.title: India's Digital Public Infrastructure Fuels E-commerce Platform Growth
forces.description: India's advanced Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), including Aadhaar, UPI, DigiLocker, and Account Aggregator, combined with affordable connectivity and a young digital consumer base, provides a powerful catalyst for platform-led retail. These foundational elements enable seamless digital interactions, payments, and data exchange, creating an environment where e-commerce, quick commerce, and social commerce can scale rapidly. This unique convergence positions India to lead global retail transformation, significantly benefiting platform-based digital commerce by reducing friction and expanding market reach.
forces.source_title: From commerce to platform : Reimagining retail as an intelligent ecosystem

forces.title: E-commerce Platforms Diversify Revenue with Adjacent Services
forces.description: Leading retailers, including e-commerce platforms, are increasingly generating substantial revenues from diversified streams beyond traditional merchandise sales. These include retail media, digital advertising, embedded financial services, subscriptions, marketplace commissions, fulfillment services, loyalty ecosystems, and data-driven insights. These adjacent revenue engines often yield higher margins and simultaneously deepen customer engagement. For e-commerce and digital commerce platforms, this diversification strategy offers a significant upside, enhancing profitability and strengthening competitive positioning by creating multiple points of value across the customer journey and ecosystem.
forces.source_title: From commerce to platform : Reimagining retail as an intelligent ecosystem

forces.title: AI Transforms Automotive Retail, Shifting to Data-Centric Mobility
forces.description: The automotive retail sector, including auto marketplaces (a sub-segment of IN040403), is experiencing a profound transformation driven by AI. This shift moves beyond mere product-centric sales to data-centric mobility, where customer intelligence, predictive engagement, and continuous relationships are paramount. AI applications are emerging around the vehicle, influencing how it is sold, financed, serviced, charged, maintained, and retained throughout its lifecycle. This fundamental change redefines competitive advantage in automotive e-commerce, focusing on integrated digital experiences and intelligent systems for customer engagement.
forces.source_title: AI will define the next battle in automotive retail

forces.title: Rising EV Penetration Boosts Auto Marketplace Activity and Opportunities
forces.description: Electric vehicle (EV) penetration in new vehicle sales is rapidly increasing, rising from 4.8% in June 2025 to 7.75% by June 2026. This trend directly benefits the auto marketplace sub-segment of e-commerce, as the transition to EVs represents a significant market shift. Higher insured values and technology-led underwriting in the EV segment also create new opportunities, making EV sales an increasingly meaningful contributor to auto marketplace revenues. This sustained growth in EV adoption acts as a strong tailwind for digital automotive commerce platforms.
forces.source_title: Retail Health and Motor Drive Non-Life Premium in June 2026

forces.title: Intensified Regulatory Scrutiny and Penalties for Digital 'Dark Patterns'
forces.description: Digital platforms, including e-commerce, face intensified regulatory scrutiny regarding 'dark patterns'—deceptive design practices that mislead users. The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) issued guidelines in 2023, followed by a June 2025 advisory for e-commerce platforms to conduct self-assessments. Recent CCPA orders in May and June 2026 imposed monetary penalties (INR 1-5 lakh) on digital platforms for dark pattern use. The RBI has also strengthened fair marketing and UI design expectations for banks and NBFCs. This increasing regulatory focus and enforcement pose a significant key risk of fines and reputational damage for e-commerce operators.

forces.title: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) Emerges as Critical for E-commerce Visibility
forces.description: A new layer of digital marketing, Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), is emerging as critical for CPG and retail. GEO shapes how brands and products appear in AI-enabled search, AI-generated answers, and 'agentic commerce'—where AI assistants help consumers discover, compare, and buy. This shift necessitates optimizing sites for LLM readability, curating reviews, and maintaining fresh content, moving beyond traditional SEO. E-commerce platforms and brands must adapt their content and data infrastructure to boost visibility in AI-driven environments, ensuring their offerings are understood, cited, and recommended by AI assistants.
forces.source_title: AI in CPG and Retail: How Winners Are Pulling Ahead

forces.title: AI Reshapes Customer Discovery, Fostering New E-commerce Business Models
forces.description: AI is fundamentally reshaping how customers discover, compare, and navigate products, transforming the e-commerce customer journey. This extends to creating new propositions like AI-enabled direct-to-consumer models offering personalized advice and AI-first shopping agents that assist with planning, comparing, and fulfillment across channels. The shift is from isolated AI use cases to AI becoming the 'operating system' of modern retail. This structural change demands that e-commerce players reinvent their business models and integrate AI across their demand value chain, from concept to customer engagement.
forces.source_title: AI in CPG and Retail: How Winners Are Pulling Ahead

forces.title: Resale Platforms Evolve as Key E-commerce Discovery and Value Channels
forces.description: Resale is increasingly moving beyond its traditional role as a discount channel, transforming into a significant source of access, discovery, and cultural validation for luxury goods, especially bags, jewelry, and watches. Engagement with pre-owned luxury rises with affluence in both the US and China, challenging previous assumptions. This structural shift means e-commerce brands cannot ignore resale, as it increasingly determines cultural icon status and long-term value perception. Platforms must leverage resale intelligence to identify future iconic products and adapt their brand-building strategies accordingly.
forces.source_title: The State of Luxury: What US and Chinese clients reveal about the sector’s future

forces.title: Trust Deficits Pose Barrier for Scaling Resale and AI Discovery in E-commerce
forces.description: In emerging luxury markets like China, the resale market is nascent and highly trust-led. This makes overcoming trust deficits a critical challenge for scaling both resale and AI-driven discovery platforms in e-commerce. Authentication, verified partnerships, provenance, and controlled distribution are essential for maintaining brand credibility. For e-commerce operators expanding into resale or integrating AI, failure to address these trust issues through robust governance and transparent practices can significantly hinder adoption and growth, limiting the potential of these transformative digital commerce channels.
forces.source_title: The State of Luxury: What US and Chinese clients reveal about the sector’s future

forces.title: Managing AI Token Spending Critical for Cost-Effective E-commerce Scaling
forces.description: As AI scales across retail and e-commerce operations, token spending and model usage can become a significant recurring operating cost. This risk is particularly acute at the 'deploy' level, where broad workforce access to AI can create material costs with diffuse productivity benefits, and in the IT function for 'reshape' activities. E-commerce leaders need clear ROI data on AI initiatives, diligent tracking of adoption and cost per utilization, and observability across the tech stack with clear cost attribution to solutions and business owners. Failure to manage this cost inflation could undermine the economic benefits of AI adoption.
forces.source_title: AI in CPG and Retail: How Winners Are Pulling Ahead

forces.title: Integrated Data Flows Essential for Agentic AI Commerce Capabilities
forces.description: The shift towards agentic AI commerce, where AI systems make autonomous decisions and interact across ecosystems, necessitates a strategic imperative for integrated data flows. While most retailers possess rich operational and customer data, much of it remains siloed. Connecting critical flows—such as loyalty IDs with POS data, e-commerce platform analytics, CRM systems, and social media data—is crucial. This integration improves visibility, builds trust, and fuels agentic AI capabilities for personalization and service improvement, transforming data governance from a defensive necessity to a value-generative capability for e-commerce platforms.
forces.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Consumer & Retail

forces.title: Major Investments by Global Players Bolster Indian E-commerce Sector
forces.description: The Indian e-commerce sector is benefiting from significant investments by global players, underscoring its high growth potential. For instance, Amazon is increasing its investment in India by US$ 15 billion over the next seven years from 2023, bringing its total investment to US$ 26 billion. Such substantial capital inflows provide crucial resources for infrastructure development, technology adoption, market expansion, and competition, acting as a strong tailwind. This enables e-commerce platforms to enhance services, expand reach, and innovate, further accelerating sector growth.

forces.title: Expanding Tier-II and Tier-III City Shopper Base Drives E-commerce Growth
forces.description: India's fastest consumer growth is originating from Tier-II and Tier-III cities, which are projected to add nearly 100 million new consumers to branded and organized retail by 2030. This expanding shopper base, characterized by increasing urbanization, rising household incomes, and connected rural consumers, fuels national consumption patterns. For e-commerce and digital commerce platforms, this demographic shift represents a significant tailwind, opening up new markets and driving demand for online retail, particularly through innovative business models and digital payments adoption in these regions.

forces.title: D2C Business Model Transforms India's Consumer Market
forces.description: The Direct-to-Consumer (D2C) business model is profoundly transforming India’s consumer market. While emerging as a concept earlier, the COVID-19 pandemic significantly accelerated its adoption, encouraging more players to leverage this model. D2C brands, which primarily operate through digital commerce, are expanding their physical presence across categories like fashion, apparel, jewelry, cosmetics, and wellness. This structural shift empowers brands to build direct relationships with customers, bypass intermediaries, and capture greater value, representing a significant new opportunity and competitive dynamic within the E-Commerce & Digital Commerce sector.

forces.title: Shift from Cash-on-Delivery to Digital Payments in E-retail
forces.description: India’s e-retail sector is witnessing a gradual, yet significant, structural shift from cash-on-delivery (COD) to digital payment modes. UPI-based payments, in particular, are gaining substantial traction across online shopping platforms and quick commerce channels. This trend is supported by the massive growth in UPI transactions (over 24,161 crore transactions worth Rs. 314 lakh crore in FY26). The increasing adoption of digital payments enhances transaction security, improves operational efficiency for platforms, and reduces logistical complexities associated with cash handling, fundamentally transforming the e-commerce payment landscape.

forces.title: Explosive Growth in UPI Transactions Boosts Digital Commerce Adoption
forces.description: The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has become a dominant force in India's digital payment ecosystem, processing over 24,161 crore transactions with a value exceeding Rs. 314 lakh crore (US$ 3553.24 billion) in FY26, accounting for ~85% of digital payment volume. This explosive growth reflects widespread adoption across retail stores, e-commerce platforms, and merchant networks. The convenience, speed, and security of UPI act as a powerful tailwind, accelerating consumer confidence in digital transactions and further driving the expansion and penetration of E-Commerce & Digital Commerce across the country.

forces.title: Consumer Demand for Mini-Sized Beauty Products Fuels E-commerce
forces.description: A notable consumer preference for mini-sized beauty products is gaining traction in India, particularly among Gen Z. This trend is driven by affordability, convenience, and the desire for experimentation, as smaller packs allow consumers to try makeup at a 'right' price point. This shift is reshaping the Indian beauty market and presents a significant tailwind for beauty e-commerce platforms. Digital channels are ideally positioned to cater to this demand, offering wide assortments, discovery features, and efficient delivery for smaller, lower-ticket items, thereby driving sales and customer engagement.

forces.title: Ethical AI Use and Data Governance Crucial for E-commerce Trust
forces.description: As e-commerce and retail companies increasingly embrace AI and agentic commerce, establishing and enforcing strong AI and data governance is paramount. Key risks include model bias, reliance on unreliable data sources, and damage to consumer trust. A robust governance model is essential for ethical AI use, ensuring transparency and drawing on reliable, authorized data. This fosters trust among consumers, regulators, and investors, providing a necessary foundation to scale AI usage and drive innovation within e-commerce. Lack of this governance poses a significant risk to reputation and adoption.
forces.source_title: KPMG 2025 Global CEO Outlook Consumer and Retail

viewpoints.title: India's Platform-Led Retail Poised for Accelerated Growth and Ecosystem Dominance
viewpoints.description: India is uniquely positioned for rapid scaling of platform-led retail due to its advanced Digital Public Infrastructure (Aadhaar, UPI, DigiLocker), affordable connectivity, and a young, digitally-savvy consumer base. The convergence of these factors, alongside the rapid rise of quick commerce, creates optimal conditions for platform businesses to thrive. Retailers are transforming from transaction-centric to relationship-centric models, orchestrating interconnected ecosystems involving consumers, brands, sellers, logistics, and financial institutions. This strategic shift facilitates value creation beyond mere transactions, leveraging network effects for sustained growth and deeper customer engagement.
viewpoints.source_title: From commerce to platform : Reimagining retail as an intelligent ecosystem

viewpoints.title: AI Interfaces: The Next Generation of Digital Storefronts for Luxury E-commerce
viewpoints.description: AI interfaces are emerging as crucial new storefronts, fundamentally reshaping how luxury consumers discover, compare, and navigate products. Brands must proactively structure content, reviews, and metadata for AI visibility to influence LLMs, which increasingly guide purchase decisions and interpret brand reputation. This shift necessitates competing for algorithmic relevance as aggressively as for cultural relevance, emphasizing investment in structured product information and authoritative content. For e-commerce, embracing AI-mediated discovery is vital for maintaining brand visibility and driving sales in an evolving digital landscape.
viewpoints.source_firm: McKinsey & Company / The Business of Fashion
viewpoints.source_title: The State of Luxury: What US and Chinese clients reveal about the sector’s future

viewpoints.title: Agentic Commerce Demands Competition for Algorithmic Preference, Not Just Customers
viewpoints.description: As consumers increasingly use AI to guide product searches and purchase decisions, e-commerce brands must adapt to an era of agentic-to-agentic commerce. This new paradigm requires businesses to compete not just for the customer's attention, but for the algorithmic preference of the AI agents consumers are utilizing. Achieving sophistication in this environment necessitates a mature AI model and overcoming hurdles such as lack of transparency, biased responses, and IP theft. Strategic data integration and ethical AI governance are crucial for success in this evolving competitive landscape.
viewpoints.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Consumer & Retail

viewpoints.title: AI Delivers Measurable ROI in Retail, Driving Efficiency and Personalization
viewpoints.description: AI is a top investment priority for consumer and retail CEOs, with 64% citing it and 73% planning to allocate 10-20% of their budget to it in the next year. This investment is yielding tangible results, with 68% expecting ROI within 1-3 years. Key benefits include efficiency and productivity gains, enhanced decision-making, and significantly increased personalization (13% of CEOs, higher than any other sector). This indicates a strong focus on leveraging AI to understand consumer preferences and lifestyles, directly impacting e-commerce platforms through improved customer experience and targeted offerings.
viewpoints.source_title: KPMG 2025 Global CEO Outlook Consumer and Retail

viewpoints.title: Nutraceuticals Sector Growth Boosts Demand for Online Delivery Platforms
viewpoints.description: India’s nutraceutical market, valued at USD 29–30 billion in 2024 and projected to reach USD 55–57 billion by 2030, is experiencing accelerated growth. A key driver for this expansion is the increasing adoption of preventive healthcare, rising health consciousness, and higher disposable incomes. The expansion of online delivery platforms is identified as a significant factor fueling demand for nutraceutical products. This trend presents a strong tailwind and demand driver for E-Commerce & Digital Commerce platforms that facilitate the delivery of health and wellness products, particularly functional foods, beverages, and dietary supplements.
